title: AI helps design new materials that work in the real world
description: The “CrysVCD” tool developed at MIT could cut the huge amounts of time and money spent on screening out chemically unstable designs.
author: Zach Winn | MIT News

title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
description: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.
author: Jennifer Chu | MIT News

title: Paving the way for greener ammonia production
description: New MIT research could lead to better materials for a fossil-fuel-free process for making the chemical that's essential to fertilizer and other products.
author: David L. Chandler | Department of Materials Science and Engineering

title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data
description: A new method for surgically removing training examples from a model reveals that as datasets grow, the link between what a model learns and what it produces dissolves.
author: Rachel Gordon | MIT CSAIL

title: Q&A: Rethinking how innovation happens
description: In his latest book, Professor Eugene Fitzgerald examines the forces that turn breakthroughs into value — and why innovation resists simple formulas.
author: Jason Sparapani | Department of Materials Science and Engineering

title: With a feel for physics, AI models simulate a wider range of real-world scenarios
description: “GeoPT” helps AI models understand the basics of physics so they can simulate how objects respond to things like wind and water more efficiently and accurately.
author: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

title: Solving the solvent problem
description: By focusing on electrolytes, MIT scientists are making sodium-metal batteries a more practical energy storage option.
author: Steve Nadis | Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering

title: The benefits of medical AI assistance vary based on user expertise
description: Study finds non-experts deferred to LLM-based diagnostic assistance, even when it was wrong, while clinicians caught AI errors.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: Alexander Rakhlin named director of the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center
description: An expert in machine learning, statistics, and computation, Rakhlin succeeds Professor Ankur Moitra.
author: Institute for Data, Systems, and Society

title: Daniela Rus receives Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize
description: Director of CSAIL and MIT professor honored for her contributions to robotics, artificial intelligence, and autonomous systems.
author: Rachel Gordon | Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

title: Connecting research to policy on Capitol Hill
description: MIT students and postdocs discussed science funding and research with policymakers in Washington during the MIT Science Policy Initiative’s annual Congressional Visit Days.
author: Science Policy Initiative

title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing
description: The visionary PhysioNet platform launched 25 years ago, based on a system developed at MIT in the 1970s. It has become one of the most comprehensive biomedical and clinical data repositories in existence.
author: Emma Foehringer Merchant | Institute for Medical Engineering and Science

title: MIT projects selected for funding under US Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission
description: Initial research projects advance national priorities across natural resources, manufacturing, nuclear physics, and more.
author: Office of the Vice President for Research

title: Professor Emeritus Dimitri Bertsekas, influential computer scientist and prolific author, dies at 83
description: Known for his clear and elegant writing style, Bertsekas shaped fields from control and optimization to large-scale computation and artificial intelligence.
author: Jane Halpern | Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science

title: Following the questions where they lead
description: Assistant Professor Bailey Flanigan has arrived at complex computational methods for helping democracy thrive.
author: Michaela Jarvis | MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

title: A better way to turn 2D designs into 3D models for rapid prototyping
description: Researchers developed an automated framework that helps AI models generate CAD programs more accurately and efficiently.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: 3 Questions: Neural transparency and the future of AI design
description: Assistant Professor Pat Pataranutaporn describes a new interface that lets everyday users glimpse inside an AI's neural network before their chatbot ever says a word.
author: Media Lab

title: Helping AI models to meet the real world
description: Through research and entrepreneurship, Professor Devavrat Shah is helping to design methods that can handle constant decision-making using limited computational resources.
author: David Chandler | Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

title: Can AI build a jet engine? JARVIS Challenge tests role of AI copilots in tough-tech engineering
description: MIT students designed, built, and tested a jet engine with AI copilots, assessing AI’s usefulness in developing high-performance aerospace systems.
author: Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics

title: How MIT students are helping to prevent cyberattacks
description: Students from the MIT Cybersecurity Clinic help local governments and other vulnerable organizations defend against digital threats.
author: Nicole Estvanik Taylor | Department of Urban Studies and Planning

title: AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data
description: “SceneSmith” system uses collaborative AI agents to create realistic 3D environments of places like kitchens, hotels, and living rooms, where robots can simulate everyday chores.
author: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

title: New method aims to keep kids safe from illegal AI-generated content
description: Researchers developed an auditing technique to test generative AI models for malicious capabilities, without prompting them for illegal outputs.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: Tiny robot boats build floating structures
description: MIT researchers developed FloatForm, a swarm of small aquatic robots that snap together like ants forming a raft, assembling into reconfigurable structures on the water.
author: Rachel Gordon | MIT CSAIL

title: How novice coders can develop AI programs for military applications
description: A USAF cadet and a Lincoln Laboratory researcher found AI chatbots can help nontechnical service members produce viable software applications for their unique problems.
author: Haley Wahl | MIT Lincoln Laboratory

title: Jesse Thaler named director of the Laboratory for Nuclear Science
description: The professor of physics and inaugural director of the NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions will lead LNS and continue his research in particle physics.
author: Julia C. Keller | School of Science

title: Toward a future that preserves benefits of neurotechnology for all
description: PhD student Rachel Sava, winner of the Envisioning the Future of Computing Prize, explores transformative improvements and dystopian risks of neural technology.
author: Amanda Diehl | MIT Schwarzman College of Computing

title: MIT in the media: Innovating and educating for the next 250 years of America
description: During a "Washington Post Live" panel discussion with ASU President Michael Crow, President Sally Kornbluth explored how universities are preparing the next generation of scientists to lead in America’s rapidly changing technological landscape.
author: MIT News AI

title: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?
description: Computer scientist Phillip Isola cuts through the hype to explain how AI agents work and what the future might hold for this rapidly advancing technology.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: Inaugural Music Technology Research Showcase celebrates work of new graduate program’s initial students
description: Associate Professor Anna Huang delivers the keynote address, “In Search of Human-AI Resonance,” to a capacity crowd.
author: Dan Pecci | MIT Music and Theater Arts

title: 3 Questions: Beyond data-driven aesthetics
description: In a new Keller Gallery exhibition, Alexandros Haridis SM ’17, PhD ’22 traces centuries of ideas about aesthetic judgment and explores how design can make complex computational systems visible.
author: School of Architecture and Planning

title: David Autor named head of the Department of Economics
description: A faculty member since 1999, Autor is a leading researcher in artificial intelligence and the work of the future.
author: Benjamin Daniel | School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences

title: LLMs help robots understand vague instructions and focus on key details
description: To help robots do chores in places like homes and factories, a new approach from MIT uses one language model to clarify users’ instructions, then another to ignore irrelevant info.
author: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

title: MIT in the media: Exploring how curiosity-driven science is an essential ingredient in America’s success
description: “Scientific American” showcases the history and future of America’s scientific engine, highlighting promising young scientists and icons at MIT and beyond.
author: MIT News AI

title: Improving the speed and energy-efficiency of AI agents
description: A new system, known as Murakkab, optimizes the design and deployment of multistep workflows that power AI applications.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: Exploring the societal impacts of AI
description: During the AI and Society Forum, leading MIT researchers examined critical questions about AI’s influence on employment and democracy.
author: Benjamin Daniel | School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences

title: New chip could help tiny robots traverse complex environments
description: Researchers combined an efficient algorithm with dedicated hardware to rapidly generate 3D maps for navigation using minimal memory and power.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: A better way to model the behavior of metal alloys
description: MIT researchers’ approach captures subtle atomic patterns, improving predictions of material properties.
author: Zach Winn | MIT News

title: MIT in the media: For the future of tech, "Massachusetts can absolutely lead"
description: Leaders, faculty across MIT discuss fostering innovation and talent in Greater Boston in special series of articles published alongside the outlet's annual list of 'Tech Power Players'
author: MIT News AI

title: In game theory, generalists sometimes win out over specialists
description: Researchers show that for certain kinds of games, an overlooked class of algorithms performs much better than expected.
author: Steve Nadis | MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

title: Could AI tell you where you left your keys?
description: A new spatial memory system for robots efficiently captures details about the objects they see while exploring their environment.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: MIT’s Initiative for New Manufacturing builds momentum
description: In its first year, INM has worked across research, workforce development, and industry engagement to help accelerate new manufacturing technologies and their real-world deployment.
author: Julie Diop | Initiative for New Manufacturing

title: Jinhua Zhao named head of the Department of Urban Studies and Planning
description: An expert in behavioral science and transportation, Zhao combines these studies with AI and public policy to address some of the most urgent challenges facing cities.
author: Maria Iacobo | School of Architecture and Planning

title: When it comes to predicting people’s preferences, it pays to consider “the power of three”
description: MIT researchers provide a major upgrade to the nearly century-old idea of random utility models.
author: Steve Nadis | MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

title: Startup’s nuclear-inspired cooling system could make data centers more sustainable
description: Founded by two researchers from MIT, Ferveret reduces the amount of energy and water required to cool the chips that power AI.
author: Zach Winn | MIT News

title: The crucial human component in computing and AI
description: The MIT Ethics of Computing Research Symposium brought together experts and researchers working at the heart of ethical and social impact in technology.
author: Amanda Diehl | MIT Schwarzman College of Computing

title: Tod Machover receives George Peabody Medal for contributions to music and technology
description: The George Peabody Medal is the highest honor bestowed by the Peabody Institute of the Johns Hopkins University.
author: Media Lab

title: MIT researchers teach AI models to interpret charts
description: The new ChartNet training dataset could improve the accuracy of vision-language models that help analyze business trends or interpret scientific figures.
author: Adam Zewe | MIT News

title: Media Advisory: MIT to establish regional quantum hub
description: With $25 million investment from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, MIT to build a new shared-use facility to serve as a statewide quantum toolbox.
author: MIT News AI

title: Technology usually creates jobs for young, skilled workers. Will AI do the same?
description: A new study of the postwar U.S. shows which kinds of workers historically filled new tech-enabled jobs.
author: Peter Dizikes | MIT News

title: Building AI models that understand chemical principles
description: Connor Coley works at the interface of chemistry and machine learning, to discover and design new drug compounds.
author: Anne Trafton | MIT News
